sources.entry: SRE cheat sheet - A cheat sheet for Site Reliability Engineering principles and numbers

summary.one_liner: A short glossary-style cheat sheet of Site Reliability Engineering terms and reference numbers, mostly drawn from Google's SRE material.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a single README that acts as a landing page for looking up SRE keywords. It defines core terms such as Site Reliability Engineering, error budget, the Four Golden Signals (saturation, latency, errors, traffic), and the difference between alerts, tickets and logs. It includes a table converting availability percentages (90% to 99.9999%) into allowed downtime per year, month and week. It also defines SLI, SLO, SLA, MTTR, MTBF, MTTF, graceful degradation, defense in depth, the Wheel of Misfortune exercise, and Capability Maturity Model. The author points readers to the Google SRE book for depth, and lists a few external links and sources at the end. Several entries, including Dickerson's Hierarchy, Postmortem, and the Additional Links, are empty or only headings.
use_cases: looking up an SRE term quickly
converting an uptime percentage into allowed downtime
explaining error budgets to a team
choosing what to monitor using the golden signals
deciding whether an event should be an alert, ticket or log
notable: Compact uptime table showing downtime per year, month and week for availability levels from 90% to 99.9999%
Defines the Four Golden Signals with latency guidance to use P50, P90 and P99 instead of averages
Covers alert, ticket and log categories for deciding how monitoring output should be handled
Mostly based on Google SRE material, with sources listed at the end
caveats: Glossary only: brief definitions, not a substitute for the Google SRE book the author recommends
Several sections are empty (Dickerson's Hierarchy, Postmortem) or only list links without descriptions
Some source citations are blank, so many claims cannot be traced from the README alone
